text:
Alex: Heads up — we're seeing a bursty latency spike and a bunch of preemptions in us-west-2 rack 12 affecting both shared and dedicated slices. Observed ~30% tail increase for short chat requests.
Priya: ugh, saw the alert. Any indication noisy neighbor (IO/egress) vs thermal?
Alex: telemetry shows sustained NIC tx spikes + GPU temperature bumps during the periods. nvlink counters also jump.
Sam: could be a background batch job on a noisy host. Which pools are getting preempted?
Alex: mostly fractional dedicated slices, but spillover into shared-slice pools when we evict. That's causing routing thrash.
Devon: do we have the soft-preempt handshake enabled for those cohorts? I think it's off in us-west-2 for preemptible allocations.
Priya: it's enabled fleet-wide but the cohort-handshake (grace window + requeue backoff) was rolled back last month in that region for perf testing.
Linh: suggestion: enable cohort-level soft-preempt handshake with a 60s grace + 90s backoff. That should reduce rapid requeue loops.
Sam: agree. If we increase backoff we avoid reassigning the same tenant into the noisy rack. Cost is slight capacity inefficiency but lowers tail.
Alex: can we canary it to 5% of preemptible traffic in us-west-2 first? want to measure egress burst tails and requeue rate.
Devon: yes. I can flip flag in allocator. Command below to patch canary label to 5%:
```
kubectl patch deploy allocator -n fleet --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/metadata/annotations/cohort-canary","value":"0.05"}]'
```
Priya: also add a metric for "requeue_same_rack_count" so we can see if tenants bounce back into the noisy rack.
Alex: good call. Sam, can you add that to the probe dashboard? small panel under Dedicated -> preemptions.
Sam: on it; will push and link in 10m.
Linh: if canary looks good, we should also tweak routing policy to prefer warm-pool allocations for tenants with >200qps until the noisy-host drains. That reduces cross-tenant interference.
Devon: routing change is more invasive; I'd rather do soft-preempt handshake + backoff first. If we still see drift after 2 hours, then routing policy.
Alex: agreed. Ops: can we throttle background batch jobs on rack 12 as emergency mitigation? @oncall-bot deploy? :fire_engine:
oncall-bot: Incident throttling play triggered for rack 12 — background batch job limiter set to 30% for best-effort workloads.
Priya: nice. keep an eye on NVLINK and NIC tx after deploy.
Sam: dashboard updated: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/egress/alloc-preemptions (panel pinned).
Linh: logging note: store the last 6 minutes of nvlink logs for the affected hosts to help model dev for noisy neighbor detection.
Alex: timeline: canary flip in 5m, monitor 30m, if requeue_same_rack_count drops >50% and tail P95 improves then roll to 50% and continue.
Devon: I'll do the flip and annotate the deploy.
Priya: thanks — and we should open a follow-up to discuss longer-term: host-level IO QoS (nic shaping) vs pool-level carveouts.
Alex: yep. I'll create a ticket after we stabilize. :thumbsup:
Devon: flipped to 5% canary — annotating: "soft-preempt-cohort-handshake canary 5% us-west-2"
oncall-bot: Deploy annotation recorded by Devon at 1812346898
Alex: monitoring — nvlink still spiky but requeue_same_rack_count down ~40% after 12m. keeping watch.
Priya: partial win. continue the plan.
Sam: if anyone sees tenant SLA regressions ping me, I'll pause the canary.
Linh: saving logs to /var/logs/noise-detection/usw2-rack12/ (6m window)
Alex: thanks team. I'll post a summary once we hit the 30m mark.
